subject: health
unitTitle: Substance Misuse Trends, Refusal Skills, and Support Pathways
title: Application or project: refusal under sustained rather than one-time pressure
focus: refusal under sustained rather than one-time pressure
essentialQuestion: How do I hold a decision when the pressure is quiet, repeated, and from someone close?
materials: guardian-approved local and national support resource list
keyPoints: Sustained pressure requires more than one refusal line: repeat the boundary, change location, contact an ally, and use a preplanned exit or ride.
A safe communication plan states the limit clearly, recognizes pressure or danger, identifies an exit, and brings in adult or professional support when direct engagement is unsafe.

For refusal under sustained rather than one-time pressure, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build a support-pathway map for three fictional situations of escalating seriousness, naming the trusted adult, the service, and the point at which emergency help is called.
studentTask: Annotate a supplied fictional exchange about refusal under sustained rather than one-time pressure: underline the stated limit, circle any pressure or respectful check-in, and write a two-sentence response that states a boundary plus a safe next step. Add when a trusted adult should enter the plan.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in refusal under sustained rather than one-time pressure; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
